PHARISEES-ERROR-SPECIFIC (vv. 5-10; expands seed 14:1 four-sectarian-errors catalog). The Pharisees' specific error: RESURRECTION-AS-CYCLIC-REINCARNATION rather than once-for-all bodily-resurrection. The Meqabyan diagnosis of Pharisaic-error is theologically-precise (vs. the standard New-Testament characterization of Pharisees as RESURRECTION-AFFIRMERS at Acts 23:6-8): per Josephus Antiquities 18.1.3 the Pharisees believed in a SOUL-TRANSMIGRATION-INTO-NEW-BODIES doctrine resembling-but-not-identical-to bodily-resurrection. Meqabyan's polemic addresses this DOCTRINAL NUANCE: bodily-resurrection means the SAME body restored, not a NEW body to which the soul transmigrates. Per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §41: the Pharisaic-cyclical-soul doctrine resembled Greek-Platonic METEMPSYCHOSIS; Christian patristic tradition firmly distinguished bodily-resurrection from transmigration (Tertullian De Anima 28-35; Augustine City of God 22.27). Meqabyan's anti-Pharisees-polemic is therefore theologically-sophisticated rather than crude.

The cord-of-Sheol image is UNIQUE TO MEQABYAN among EOTC canonical literature: a numinous-cord physically-attached-to-the-soul from-conception that draws-the-soul into Sheol at death. Per Horovitz 1905 p. 220: the image has no direct biblical or patristic-parallel; closest analogues are: 1 SAMUEL 18:1 ('the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David' — bond-imagery for love rather than death); PSALM 18:4-5 ('the sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid. The cord-of-Sheol is one of Meqabyan's most DISTINCTIVE THEOLOGICAL IMAGES — Tewahedo preaching tradition cites 2 Mq 14:23 for the doctrine of INHERITED-MORTALITY-FROM-CONCEPTION (Adamic-mortality at ontological depth).

CLIMACTIC RESURRECTION-THESIS STATEMENT (vv. 29-36): the chapter's anti-sectarian polemic-architecture climaxes in a POSITIVE-FORMULATION of the four-fold doctrine: (1) bodily resurrection of the SAME body; (2) of ALL the dead — righteous and wicked; (3) by GOD'S POWER ALONE; (4) leading to ETERNAL judgment-and-reward. The four-fold-formulation parallels: DANIEL 12:2 ('many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt' — TWO-FOLD-RESURRECTION); JOHN 5:28-29 ('the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation' — Johannine TWO-FOLD-RESURRECTION); ACTS 24:15 ('there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust' — Pauline-Lukan formula); REVELATION 20:11-15 (great-white-throne judgment after first-and-second-resurrections). Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the FOUR-FOLD formulation EXPLICITLY ADDS that resurrection is OF THE SAME BODY (anti-Pharisaic-transmigration) and BY GOD'S POWER ALONE (anti-Sadducean-naturalism).

FOUR-ELEMENTS RESURRECTION — Adam's body composed of earth + water + fire + wind, returned to its elements at death, and reconstituted at resurrection by God's gathering of those elements. Direct parallel to 3 Mq 4:10 (where the same anthropology is given in the creational rather than resurrectional context). The four-elements doctrine is the EMPEDOCLEAN/GALENIC Greek natural-philosophical anthropology, mediated to Ethiopian Christianity via Syriac and Coptic patristic literature (Ephrem Carmina Nisibena 65; Severus of Antioch Cathedral Homilies). The resurrection-by-elemental-reconstitution-doctrine is also in Tertullian De Resurrectione Carnis §52 + Theophilus of Antioch Ad Autolycum 1.13 (per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX Stage-3 broadening at 2 Mq 17). The chapter's CORD-OF-SHEOL image (vv. 10-23) — the bond dragging soul to Hades grows from mother's womb up through life — is a unique metaphor in EOTC literature.
